root_motivation: Agents and assistants cannot query homeward: the database is live on the hub but reachable only via the wall UI (:8090) and the report API (:8081) — neither speaks MCP, so the fastest-growing consumer surface (agent tool use) has zero access. Evidence: homeward-ops service inventory (verified 2026-08-31); no MCP component exists in the repo; five prior `*-mcp` PRDs in built-prds/ establish the local pattern (recall-mcp, muster-mcp, docket-mcp, provenance-mcp, mdcollab-mcp).
user_persona: UNSPECIFIED — no existing intent card to carry forward from; set by hand (intent-card-refresh.sh cannot source this from a PRD).

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the server on stdio with a fixture DB, When a client calls tools/list, Then exactly search_pets and get_pet appear with JSON schemas and recent_intakes lists as a resource.

Given fixture intakes near location X, When search_pets(dog, X, 50km) is called, Then only in-radius dogs return, each with hotlinked photo URL, coarse location, and brokered shelter contact — and no person-level PII field exists in the payload.
Given a search with no matches, When called, Then an empty result with a well-formed shape returns (no error, no nulls where lists belong).
Given an invalid species value, When search_pets is called, Then a typed MCP error returns and the server stays up.
Given the DB file is absent, When any tool is called, Then a clean typed error returns (no traceback in the client payload) and the process does not exit.
Given the same entry point, When started with --http, Then the same tool calls succeed over streamable HTTP as over stdio.
Given a 60k-row fixture DB, When 200 timed search_pets calls run, Then p95 < 200 ms.
Given 20 concurrent HTTP clients for 60 s, When they issue mixed tool calls, Then zero errors and no request starves >2 s.
Given the deploy recipe, When applied on a hub-like environment, Then a homeward-mcp user unit runs alongside the existing four services' conventions.
